title: Multi-tenant SLO escalation and SLA credit playbook
author: Alexandra Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the escalation paths, operational actions, and SLA credit calculation methodology for multi-tenant SLO degradations affecting Redwood Inference hosted customers. It is intended for on-call SREs, customer success managers (CSMs), account owners, and billing ops. The guidance covers immediate triage, customer communications, attribution rules across multi-tenant incidents, and the formal SLA credit calculation & approval flow.

Scope:
- Applies to incidents where a single platform condition or gradual degradation impacts two or more paid hosted customers (not Dedicated or Private tenants).
- Excludes customer-side misconfigurations (eg, misrouted VPC, client rate-limiter misconfiguration) unless Redwood confirms root cause.

Objectives:
- Restore SLOs quickly with clear ownership split between SRE and Customer Success.
- Communicate transparently to affected customers within defined windows.
- Calculate and issue SLA credits consistently and auditable for billing.

Definitions and thresholds:
- SLO types: P99 latency (<= 600ms), Availability (>= 99.95% per 30d), Streaming Throughput (tokens/sec target).
- Severity levels (applies when >= 2 tenants affected):
  - Sev2: Major SLO breach impacting customer experience but with partial functionality (eg increased P99 latency >1.5x baseline).
  - Sev1: Platform-wide availability impacting request success rate (>5% error rate over 15m) or sustained availability <99.5%.
- Breach windows: Use rolling 15m, 1h, and 24h windows to determine incident length.

Ownership matrix:
- Primary: SRE (platform remediation, runbooks, telemetry).
- Secondary: Customer Success (customer comms, impact assessment, liaison to billing/legal).
- Tertiary: Product/Runtime Eng (model routing/variant configuration if needed).

Escalation matrix (quick reference):
1) Detection: Alert triggers (SLO alert, customer complaint routed to CS).
2) Triage (15 minutes): On-call SRE owner acknowledges alert (PagerDuty). If >=2 tenants referenced in alerts or top-down degradation metrics show multi-tenant impact --> declare Multi-tenant Incident.
3) Notification (30 minutes): CS lead runs affected-customer query and initiates templated comms (see "Customer comms templates" section).
4) Exec escalation (60 minutes for Sev1, 180 minutes for Sev2): Notify on-call director, customer success director, and designated account owners.

Immediate triage checklist (first 30 minutes):
- Confirm scope: run tenant-aggregation query (example BigQuery/ClickHouse):
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS errors, sum(tokens) as tokens FROM request_events WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '15' minute GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY errors DESC LIMIT 50;
- Verify whether issue maps to: routing layer, kernel OOMs, autoscaler thrash, upstream cloud networking (AZ-level), model variant fallback loops, or a storage backend (KV cache) outages.
- If routing or model variant related: temporarily route affected customers to compatible model variant via routing policy (rollback plan pre-approved).
- If resource saturation: trigger capacity-burst escalation (eng-sre runbook "capacity-surge-degraded-throughput"), and consider temporary rate-limits per-tenant to buy stabilization time.

Customer communication templates (use GitHub snippet for copy/paste):
- Initial notification (short):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Investigation under way for service degradation
  Body: We are investigating an issue affecting model inference latency/availability for a subset of hosted customers. Our SRE and CS teams are engaged. We will provide an update within 30 minutes and an estimated remediation ETA within 60 minutes.
- Follow-up (impact summary):
  Subject: Incident update — platform impact and next steps
  Body: Current status: {summary}. Affected tenants: {tenant list}. Mitigation in progress: {actions}. Next update: {time}. If you need immediate assistance, contact: {CS contact + escalation phone}.
- Post-incident summary and credit notice:
  Subject: Incident report and SLA credit for {month}
  Body: Root cause, duration, impact per tenant, SLA credit calculation (see attached table), and instructions to apply credit on next invoice.

SLA credit calculation methodology:
- Principles:
  - Credits are applied only when Redwood is the root cause.
  - For multi-tenant incidents, credits are proportional to the customer’s measured impact window, not the number of tenants.
  - Credits are capped at the maximum defined in customer contract (commonly 100% of monthly service fee for the affected product line).

- Inputs required:
  - Baseline: Customer's monthly hosted API fee (M).
  - Impact fraction: Fraction of time within the billing period the customer experienced a confirmed SLO breach attributable to Redwood (F). F is expressed in hours / total hours in billing period.
  - Severity multiplier: Sm = 1.0 for Sev2, 1.5 for Sev1.

- Formula:
  Credit = min(M * F * Sm, ContractMax)

- Example table (ASCII):
  | Example: Tenant A | Value | Notes |
  | ------------------ | ----- | ----- |
  | Monthly fee (M)    | $5,000| Subscription for hosted API tier |
  | Confirmed impact   | 12 hours | Measured in rolling windows across month |
  | Billing period hrs | 720 hrs| 30-day period |
  | Impact fraction (F)| 12/720 = 0.0167 | |
  | Severity multiplier (Sm)| 1.5 | Sev1 sustained outage |
  | Calculated credit  | $5,000 * 0.0167 * 1.5 = $125.25 | Rounded to $125.25 |
  | Contract max       | $5,000 | Unused cap |
  | Final credit issued| $125.25 | Apply as invoice adjustment or one-time credit |

Attribution & evidence collection (auditability):
1) For each impacted tenant assemble a single CSV with columns: tenant_id, start_iso, end_iso, metric (latency|errors), metric_value, root_cause_tag, evidence_snapshot_url.
2) Evidence must include: dashboard snapshots (15m, 1h, 24h), request-level logs for sample requests (redact PII), and routing config state at time of incident.
3) Store evidence bundle in shared incident folder (internal GCS path) and link from post-incident report.

Approval and credit issuance flow:
1) CS drafts post-incident report and computes provisional credits for affected tenants.
2) Billing Ops validates contract caps and posts a provisional credit memo in billing queue within 7 business days.
3) Finance approves and issues final credit within 14 business days; CSM communicates credit to customer and confirms invoice adjustment.

Edge cases and special handling:
- Overlapping incidents: If multiple Redwood incidents overlap, credits are calculated for each incident independently and de-duplicated by time window in the billing system (billing ops rule: highest single-credit per time window applies).
- Partial attribution (customer-side contributing factor): Credits are proportionally reduced by documented customer contribution percentage (documented in evidence bundle).
- Dedicated/Private tenants: Follow the Dedicated/Private escalation and crediting process (refer to "enterprise-onboarding/dedicated-tenant-cutover-safety-net-playbook-2026").

Post-incident actions (within 7 days):
- Root cause analysis (RCA): Draft by owning engineering team with remediation and timeline for fixes.
- Customer QBR follow-up: For accounts with >$20k/mo or strategic importance, schedule a technical QBR within 30 days to review improvements and avoid recurrence.
- Runbook updates: If the incident exposed a gap in runbooks, update the relevant SRE and CS procedures and label the change as "required by incident".

Telemetry queries & dashboards (examples):
- Service-level latency summary (15m, 1h, 24h): use prebuilt Grafana dashboard 'multi-tenant-slo-rollups'.
- Per-tenant error rate: SELECT tenant_id, count_if(code >= 500)/count(*) FROM request_events WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 100;

Communication & escalation contact list (redacted placeholder contacts — store actual contacts in team vault):
- On-call SRE: pager (primary), slack: #oncall-sre
- CS lead: pager (secondary), slack: #cs-critical
- Billing ops: email billing-ops@redwood.ai

Appendix A — Templates for billing memo (CSV columns):
- tenant_id, invoice_period_start, invoice_period_end, calculated_credit_usd, link_to_evidence, approver_id

Appendix B — Approval checklist for issuing credit:
- Evidence bundle attached (Y/N)
- Contract caps verified (Y/N)
- Finance approval timestamp
- CSM notification recorded (Y/N)

Related runbooks and docs:
- capacity-surge-degraded-throughput-playbook-2026 (eng-sre)
- incident-process/postmortem-template-2025 (oncall-and-incident-response)
- enterprise-onboarding/dedicated-tenant-cutover-safety-net-playbook-2026 (customer-success-and-support)

Notes & governance:
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly by CS and EngSRE leadership. Any change to the SLA credit formula requires approval from Finance and Legal.
